chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him: Do the maternal brothers have any share of the blood money (diyah)? He said: 'No.'

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: Blood money (compensation paid for death or injury)
key_terms.الْإِخْوَةِ مِنَ الْأُمِّ: Maternal brothers (siblings sharing the same mother but different fathers)

ai.seo_question: Do maternal brothers inherit blood money (diyah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that maternal brothers (*ikhwān al-umm*) are excluded from inheriting the blood money (*diyah*) of their deceased sibling, a ruling that distinguishes them from full or paternal brothers who hold this right. This specific legal nuance highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that *diyah* inheritance follows the rules of *'aṣabah* (agnatic kinship) rather than the broader inheritance shares assigned in the Quran, thereby limiting the right to those with a stronger paternal lineage. The ruling underscores the precision of Imami fiqh in differentiating between general inheritance rights and the specific entitlements of blood money among various categories of relatives.
